subject.title: agentmemory__memory_search returns "index metadata is missing" persistently (memory-core manager state cache)

question: After persisted `memorySearch` provider, model, remote, or scope settings change, should a running gateway reload and replace its memory manager, or should it require a gateway restart and return that explicit action?
rationale: The reports establish that rebuilding the SQLite index cannot repair a gateway using an older configuration snapshot. Choosing automatic reload versus a clear restart boundary changes runtime configuration semantics and cannot safely be inferred from the bug report alone.

options.title: Explicit restart boundary
options.body: Keep memory-manager settings boot-scoped and replace the misleading reindex action with a precise gateway-restart requirement after settings drift.

options.title: Lifecycle-owned hot reload
options.body: Add a gateway configuration-change lifecycle that evicts and rebuilds the affected memory manager using the current canonical settings.

options.title: Narrow diagnostic only
options.body: First surface the stale settings fingerprint and provider failure clearly, then defer reload behavior until the wider gateway configuration policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Explicit restart boundary
recommendation.body: Keep memory-manager settings boot-scoped and replace the misleading reindex action with a precise gateway-restart requirement after settings drift.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related repair work is closest to the live manager/database cache boundary implicated by the original report.
